AFL Trade Period live updates: Zak Butters, Zach Merrett and Ben King among stars on the move
The AFL trade period officially opens as stars like Zak Butters, Zach Merrett and Ben King chase blockbuster moves.

Scott Pendlebury's trade to Gold Coast agreed
This one hasn't been fully ticked and completed yet, but it won't be far off.
Cal Twomey of AFL.com.au reports that the deal will be Scott Pendlebury to Gold Coast for pick 65. Expect that one to go through officially later today.
Trade confirmed: Jesse Hogan to Collingwood
There we go, the first trade of 2026 is locked in.
Jesse Hogan is a Magpie, and GWS has picked up pick 75 in return.
That's club number four for Hogan, who will be 32 at the start of next season.
Swans do not expect any of the banned players to leave
Sydney's head of list strategy and player personnel Chris Keane is up now, and was asked if he expects the five banned players to stay at the club.
"Yeah I do, they're contracted players and required players. We've had no indication that any of them are seeking other opportunities."
A Zak Butters update from the Western Bulldogs
The list bosses are arriving and speaking to Trade Radio and wider media as they come through. First up is Michael Regan, the Bulldogs' player acquisition and strategy manager.
Naturally, he's speaking about Zak Butters primarily:

"There are multiple levers we can pull to get a deal done. First up is Port deciding if they want the compensation pick. They have wanted an indication on what we are prepared to do should they not accept the compensation pick. We've given them all the information we can to make the best decision for their club.
"We've got multpile priorities this year and into the future, so we need to structure this in the best way possible for us.
"We've had good preliminary discussions with Port Adelaide."
He also confirmed there is interest in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness.
Butters, Marshall and some scuppered shenanigans
What are your thoughts on the proposed involvement of Todd Marshall in the Zak Butters trade, and Ports "Pick Purchasing" - Oscar
What are your thoughts on the proposed involvement of Todd Marshall in the Zak Butters trade, and Ports "Pick Purchasing"
A reminder of the deal the Dogs and Power tried to orchestrate:

Port was going to let Zak Butters go to the Bulldogs as a free agent, netting pick five as compensation. Then, in a nominally separate deal, Todd Marshall was going to head to the Bulldogs (with Port covering a portion of his salary) in return for numerous first round picks from the Bulldogs.
It was a way of inflating the Zak Butters deal for Port Adelaide, but the AFL shut it down, banning clubs from covering the salary of departing players if another player moved between the same clubs.
Confused? That was kinda the idea.

It was definitely a loophole in the system and you can understand why fans and rival clubs were unhappy. Personally, I think the AFL keeps getting itself into these messes by fixing problems on the run, with one closed loophole only ever opening up another one.

Clubs are going to keep trying to manipulate and benefit from the league's free agency system, which is imperfect. The clubs seem to be ahead of the league in terms of finding these imperfections, which is leading to situations like these and outcomes nobody is really happy with.
Zach Merrett chat returns!

Hi Dean, love the ABC trade blog every year. What are your thoughts on Andrew Walsh's comments around the Merrett trade? Essendon botched it last year; surely trying to play hardball now could come back to bite them. - Sarah

Hi Dean, love the ABC trade blog every year. What are your thoughts on Andrew Walsh's comments around the Merrett trade? Essendon botched it last year; surely trying to play hardball now could come back to bite them.
- Sarah
It feels like Essendon have set themselves on a compensation pick around pick 30 in next years draft for Zack Merrett - Richard
It feels like Essendon have set themselves on a compensation pick around pick 30 in next years draft for Zack Merrett
- Richard
It's that time of year again! Get the big top up, the Zach Merrett Circus is back in town.
First of all, here is what Essendon presiden Andrew Welsh told News Corp recently about Merrett, Hawthorn, last year and this year:

"Hawthorn wouldn't want to fumble or try to get too cute with us again in their approach to the negotiations. "What transpired last year and the strategy they implemented to try and force a deal through wasn't successful and it won't be again this year. We won't be crumbling. "Zach is our best player, a contracted player, so let's wait and see what Hawthorn's approach is this time."
"Hawthorn wouldn't want to fumble or try to get too cute with us again in their approach to the negotiations.
"What transpired last year and the strategy they implemented to try and force a deal through wasn't successful and it won't be again this year. We won't be crumbling.
"Zach is our best player, a contracted player, so let's wait and see what Hawthorn's approach is this time."
In my view, Essendon didn't botch it last year. I think 12 months ago the Bombers were right to hold their ground.

This year, I think a deal has to get done. I understand Welsh setting the scene with some tough words before it all kicks off but it is in nobody's interests for Merrett to be held to the last year of his contract this time around.

This is Essendon's last chance to load up on draft picks for Merrett and I'm almost certain they will take that chance. What they lose in experience they may very well make back up in the form of Jack Viney and, to a lesser extend, Jack Bowes.
There will be more posturing and bickering, but it will happen this time around.
Key Event
Jesse Hogan close to Collingwood
We're expecting this one to be officially confirmed later today.
Riley Beveridge from AFL.com.au has reported that the Giants have reached a deal though, in which the Giants will receive pick 75 from the Magpies for Jesse Hogan.
Interest in Keidean Coleman?
What teams could you foresee reaching out to Brissy RE Coleman? Understand there are some big injury concerns, but he was 2min away from a Norm Smith and is still relatively young - gREGG
What teams could you foresee reaching out to Brissy RE Coleman? Understand there are some big injury concerns, but he was 2min away from a Norm Smith and is still relatively young
- gREGG

No clubs have been linked to Coleman just yet, but there are plenty of clubs who could use him. Some obvious ones would be Richmond (especially if Jayden Short leaves) or Melbourne (especially if Trent Rivers leaves), but that is just totally random spitballing.
The knees are a concern of course so there is an element of risk there, but he has proven that when fit he is an incredibly damaging half-back who would be best 23 at most clubs in the league.
A Giant exodus
GWS look like they are losing a lot of players. Any idea who might be coming into the club to fill those holes? - Nervous
GWS look like they are losing a lot of players. Any idea who might be coming into the club to fill those holes?
- Nervous
A lot of experience and star power is heading out the door at GWS, and it doesn't look like a whole lot is coming in via trade to replace them.

The Giants will be looking to the draft this year, and will surely be looking to improve their hand to bring in multiple high-end picks. Ethan Matthews is one out of their academy, a fantastic midfield prospect who should get a bid in the top 10, but they will want and need more than that.
The Sydney situation
Dean, what is your assessment of the reported exodus from the Swans following the Pullman incident? - Neil
Dean, what is your assessment of the reported exodus from the Swans following the Pullman incident?
- Neil

There is clearly a lot to play out on this front, not least because the police investigation into those four Swans players is ongoing and is unlikely to be completed before the end of the trade period.

We have heard very little from or about the players and their intentions beyond this year, for obvious reasons. There has been some suggestion reported over the past couple of weeks that Nick Blakey would be interested in exploring a move away from Sydney, but nothing has been formalised on that front yet.

Chad Warner is another name mentioned, but West Coast list manager Matt Clarke last week said he felt Warner wanted to stay at Sydney next year for what would be the final year of his contract. The Eagles no doubt will have strong interest in Warner as a free agent this time next year and likely asked tentative questions this year, but it looks like Warner will be staying put.

It's such a tricky and sensitive situation, uncharted waters in many ways for the Swans and other clubs looking at these players. It is clearly not the most important part of this whole story, but it is a subplot that is still developing.
The Lion sleeps this trade period
Hi Dean, do you see much happening for the lions this trade period? - Damien
Hi Dean, do you see much happening for the lions this trade period?
- Damien

I wouldn't be expecting too much activity out of Brisbane in this trade period. Zac Bailey is locked in, Lachie Neale is gone, but there is a watch on Kiddy Coleman who is reportedly interested in a move elsewhere.

Brisbane's biggest mission over the next month and a bit will be putting themselves in a position to match a bid on draft night for academy prospect Caylen Murray. Murray is an electric rebounding half-back (and potential Coleman replacement) who is likely to attract a bid just outside the top 10. As it stands, it'll be touch-and-go whether the Lions could match a bid that high so they will need to put some work into their draft hand.
Richmond's days ahead
Hello my fellow Dean, love your work, Whats an ideal trade period look like for richmond and what do you think we would get for short? Cheers Dean - Dean
Hello my fellow Dean, love your work, Whats an ideal trade period look like for richmond and what do you think we would get for short? Cheers Dean
- Dean
Hello Dean. I didn't mention Jayden Short in the previous post on Collingwood, but it does seem like he is another one in the Magpies' crosshairs.

I don't think the Tigers would be getting a whole lot back if Short was to ask to head to the Pies. Best case would probably be their second round pick (currenly 28 but would blow well into the 30s). A Jayden Short bidding war would probably be the best result for the Tigers. Or convincing him to stay, that's probably the play.

Looks like Richmond will be relatively quiet aside from that. If I was them, I would be looking at options at finding another early pick in this year's draft, even so much as contemplating trading a 2027 first rounder to make it happen.

Then they need to decide what to go for with pick two in the draft. Do they go the unique ruck prospect in Harry van Hattum? The dangerous forward/mid hybrid Arki Butler? Or a more genuine midfielder like Ethan Drever or Heath Mellody? One of those players will be off the board by their pick, but they have a big decision ahead from the others.
Collingwood making moves
One down, at least a couple to go for the Pies.

Two-time Brownlow Medallist Lachie Neale is a Magpie, with that move confirmed on Friday when the free agency window opened. Neale joins Nick Daicos in what must now be considered one of the very best midfields in the AFL.

Next up is almost certainly going to be Jesse Hogan, who will probably join the Magpies today. The former Coleman Medallist is on his way from the Giants for a late pick. If he can get fit, that could be another significant addition for the Collingwood forward line.

Then there's Flynn Riley, a ruck who was picked up by Carlton in the midseason draft this year but who has asked for a trade to the Magpies. He may not move the needle a whole lot, but it's still Collingwood getting one over Carlton, which isn't nothing I guess.
The Pies have an early draft pick in a tasty range in this year's draft too, and that is unlikely to be moved.
Enough to make the Pies a 2027 contender?
Saints to play hardball over Rowan Marshall?

Do you think Geelong would be willing to send Jay Polkinghorne and pick 14 to Moorabbin as part of a trade for Rowan Marshall, possibly also with pick 8, given that St Kilda need a key forward and are insisting on getting a player in return? - Adam

Do you think Geelong would be willing to send Jay Polkinghorne and pick 14 to Moorabbin as part of a trade for Rowan Marshall, possibly also with pick 8, given that St Kilda need a key forward and are insisting on getting a player in return?
- Adam
First of all to set the scene, reports emerged last night that St Kilda was looking for Geelong's pick 14 AND a player for ruck Rowan Marshall.
That to me seems like obvious overs, and the Cats won't be doing that. Also don't think the Saints will be too keen to part with pick eight and certainly not for Jay Polkinghorne in this instance.

Geelong's first two picks are currently 14 and 34. The Cats probably say 14 is too much and the Saints would say 34 isn't enough. The answer might have to be in the middle, but how do they make that happen?

The Cats are also on the hook for Jordan Ridley from Essendon, and it sounds like they will be offering future picks for that deal. They are going to have to come up with something (and give up something) to get both of those deals done.
All the list bosses are (almost) here
As is tradition on the first day of the trade period, every single club's list manager will pass through the media zone and take a few questions as the big meetings get underway.
Looks like they'll be coming through in reverse alphabetical order (Western Bulldogs first, Adelaide last) from 11am AEDT through to about 1pm AEDT.
No doubt lots of people will be working through things, having open discussions, won't be ruling anything out and will be making their positions clear.
We'll have the best bits from all of those when they happen.
What are we looking out for today?

Trade period is open until 8pm AEDT next Wednesday (October 14), and rest assured plenty of deals will run all the way up to that deadline. But there is too much to do for it all to get left to the last minute.

On my list, I had more than 50 players potentially looking at moves in this trade period. Some of those have already completed FA moves, some have signed new contracts at their exisiting clubs, but most are up in the air. Here are some of the big ones we're watching for:
• Zak Butters to the Western Bulldogs - Will they cook up something interesting (or dodgy?) with the free agency compo pick?
• Zach Merrett to Hawthorn - The Bombers have already turned down an offer. Will this one go to the wire again?
• Ben King to Hawthorn - Surely a pretty straightforward one.
• Lachie Whitfield to Carlton - As above
• Rowan Marshall to Geelong - Saints want a king's ransom. Cats are the toughest negotiators in town.
• Jordan Ridley to Geelong - As above, but swap the Saints for the Bombers.
• Jack Viney to Essendon or West Coast - Sophie's choice!
And much, much more. That hasn't even scratched the surface. We've got a long way to go and a lot to cover!
Key Event
The deals that have already been done
While the trade period only officially opened today, the free agency period actually began on Friday, so free agents have been able to move clubs since then.
In those three days, we saw a handful of players switch clubs. It just so happens that some of those players were genuine stars of the game. Here's what you might have missed:
• Lachie Neale to Collingwood (Lions receive band three compensation)
• Toby Greene to Geelong (Giants receive band three compensation)
• Joel Amartey to Carlton (Swans receive band three compensation)
• Jordon Butts to Western Bulldogs (Crows receive band three compensation)
• Kieren Briggs to Richmond (Giants receive band four compensation)
Not a bad start to the window.

If you're wondering, "band three compensation" means a draft pick after the club's natural second round pick. So the Giants got pick 26 for Greene, the Swans pick 37 for Amartey etc. Band four is the same thing, but in the third round of draft picks.

There was some surprise and disappointment from the Giants, Lions and Crows in the outcome as each were hoping for a band two compensation pick (which would have come at the end of the first round). Seems to me the AFL is trying to water down free agency compensation a little this year.
Key Event
Welcome to AFL trade period

Good morning, and welcome to the opening day of the 2026 AFL trade period. Barely a week after Brisbane's incredible triumph in this year's grand final, attentions are already turning to 2027 and beyond as clubs begin wheeling and dealing in the hopes of building their next premiership side.

The trade period is open until next Wednesday and you can rely on me and Chris De Silva (when he returns from his post-season jollies) to bring you all of the news, all of the worthwhile rumours, all the machinations and drama and brinkmanship, all of the draft analysis and all of the fun involved with this time of the year.
Can't wait to do it all again. Hit us up with your thoughts and questions and let's get this trade period up and running.
